Chapter 10. The Ongoing Struggle for Humanity.
Rwanda’s path after the genocide has been anything but simple. There’s been progress—roads patched up, schools bustling with kids again, and fresh businesses popping up around the country. The government’s been working hard to bring people together, encouraging unity and reconciliation. But those old wounds aren’t easy to forget. They’re still there, just beneath the surface.
Picture this—a young entrepreneur, born after the genocide, starts a small business in Kigali. She’s got this drive to make things better, so she hires both survivors and former perpetrators. She wants everyone to have a shot at something new. Her energy catches on, and soon her business stands as a beacon of hope for the whole community.
Still, it’s not all smooth sailing. Poverty, deep-seated trauma, and mistrust haven’t disappeared. Some neighborhoods find it tough to let go of the past, and the road toward true reconciliation is unpredictable. There are good days and setbacks, and the process just keeps unfolding.
Meanwhile, the international community—still stung by its failure in Rwanda—tries to do better. They’re putting new policies in place, rethinking peacekeeping, and working harder to avoid the same mistakes. But let’s be honest, there’s always the danger of slipping back into inaction, so staying alert is more important than ever.
Take the story of a former aid worker. Now, she’s with a human rights organization, traveling to some of the world’s toughest conflict zones. She carries Rwanda’s lessons with her, determined to make a real difference this time. She knows this work never truly ends, but she believes change is within reach.
So, what’s the heart of Rwanda’s story? It’s about loss, yes, but it’s also about resilience and hope. The people who survived the genocide still bear the scars, but they’ve found the strength to rebuild, to move forward. Their courage shows us just how powerful the human spirit can be.
